text:
### Observed differences

- Participation shifted markedly for several activities. In the earlier window, A01 appeared in about 32 of 100 traces, A03 and A10 in every trace, A04 in about 37 and A12 in about 15; A08 and A09 never occurred. In the later window, A01 is absent from all 200 traces, A08 appears in about 48 of 100 and A09 in about 18, A03 and A10 each appear in only about 50 of 100, and A04 and A12 rose to about 52 and 48 of 100. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- A03 and A10 changed from being executed together to being alternatives. Earlier they co-occurred in 100 of 100 traces (with A07 preceding them in about 80 of 100); in the later window every trace contains exactly one of the two — A03 in about 50 of 100, A10 in about 50 of 100, never both. [REL012, REL009, OCC002, OCC006]
- A06 (about 25 of 100 traces before, 18 after) previously led mostly to A07 (about 73 of its observed outgoing transitions) or A10 (about 18); in the later window it leads exclusively to the new A09, which sits early in the trace (median position about 0.2) and leads mostly onward to A07 (about 89 of its outgoing transitions). [DIR002, REL015, POS004, DIR004]
- The new A08 runs near the end of the trace (median position about 1.0) in about 48 of 100 later traces, always together with A12 and typically after A07 (about 48 of 100 traces); A08's observed outgoing transitions all go to A12 and A12's all go to A08, with both orders observed (A12 first in about 30 of 100, A08 first in about 18 of 100). [OCC004, POS003, REL023, REL018, DIR003, DIR006]
- A01's former role has disappeared: before, A01 always co-occurred with A07, which preceded it, typically as the final event of the trace, and A01 was a successor of A03 (about 16 of A03's outgoing transitions) and A10 (about 15); in the later window A01 is unobserved and no longer appears among the successors of A03 or A10, which now lead mainly to A04, A12 and A07. [REL003, POS001, DIR001, DIR005, OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural reorganisation of the control flow involving A01, A03, A10, A06 and the two new activities A08 and A09. In the earlier window every case ran A07 followed by both A03 and A10, about 32 of 100 cases continued to A01 as the final step, and A06 occasionally fed into A07 or A10; in the later window A01 is unobserved, A03 and A10 have become exclusive alternatives of which each case executes exactly one, A06 leads only into the new A09 — which runs early and continues to A07 — and the new A08 runs near the end, always paired with A12 and usually after A07. The hypothesis is supported directly: participation counts show the addition and removal outright (A08 in 0 of 200 traces before versus 96 of 200 after; A01 in 64 versus 0), successor profiles show the new routing (A06 now leads only to A09; A08 and A12 point only at each other), and the relation and gap items change consistently with this picture. With 49 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected if nothing had changed, sampling variation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL003, REL009, REL012, REL015, REL018, REL023, DIR002, DIR003, DIR006, POS003, POS004, screening]

An important competing explanation remains: the even split between A03 and A10 in the later window could also reflect a mixture of two coexisting process variants rather than a single changed process, and because the activity codes are anonymous, a relabelling of existing activities (rather than genuinely new ones) cannot be excluded. [REL012, DIR003, DIR006]

Other differences: A04 now appears in about 52 of 100 traces (about 37 before); A07 tends to sit slightly later in the trace (median event position 0.4 to 0.5); several pairs that previously showed mixed one- or two-step gaps (A07–A10, A07–A03, A03–A07) are now always adjacent, while the A06–A10 gap lengthened to about three steps. [OCC003, POS002, LAG001, LAG004, LAG005, LAG003]
